entries.title: OpenAI rolls out its merged ChatGPT Chat and Work tabs, with a shared usage meter, to a small group of Pro users, saying heavy users may hit their limits sooner (Jagmeet Singh/TechCrunch)
Investigation: Nvidia sells its most advanced chips to at least two Chinese-owned California companies, which have leased or sold some of them to firms in Asia (Josh Boswell/CBS News)
Apple removes MiniMax's chatbot Talkie from the App Store worldwide over sexual content, after outlets showed it evidence of AI characters sexualizing children (TBIJ)
Neuralink says it got FDA approval for the LINK Pivotal Study, a US clinical trial to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of its BCI system in ALS patients (Craig Trudell/Bloomberg)
A US court dismisses Amazon's challenge to a 2025 CPSC order requiring it to recall 400K+ hazardous products sold by third parties via Fulfillment by Amazon (Emma Roth/The Verge)
A coalition of 42 AGs opposes Character.AI's plan to auction off data from 21M+ US accounts, 2.1M+ registered to minors, saying the sale lacks user protections (Sarah Perez/TechCrunch)
Hands-on with the "Install as app" feature for Claude artifacts: they are HTML apps wrapped inside an Electron shim, which is managed via the main Claude app (Federico Viticci/MacStories)
Sources: Pete Hegseth and other Pentagon officials discussed using the Defense Production Act as leverage to pressure Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang (Washington Post)
Sources: US chip curbs stall billions in data center loans tied to ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent, with some lenders delaying a $6.6B Bridge Data Centres loan (Bloomberg)
NY Gov. Kathy Hochul signs a bill banning AI chatbot toys for five years, starting in February; California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed a four-year ban in September (NBC News)
Nvidia agrees to pay $290M to settle a 2018 class action lawsuit alleging it misled shareholders about how much crypto mining fueled its GPU sales (Mike Scarcella/Reuters)
Sources: the DOJ didn't formally investigate Jensen Huang before his reinstatement; AG Todd Blanche cleared him based on probes into Super Micro and Megaspeed (Reuters)
WhatsApp starts letting users schedule messages from 10 minutes to 14 days in advance, in group and individual chats; messages are sent even if the phone is off (Ivan Mehta/TechCrunch)
Sources: a16z is in talks to raise ~$20B across its next set of funds; its last set, announced in January at $15B+, later grew to $20B+ with three add-ons (Lucinda Shen/Axios)
1Password says an attacker used an employee's GitHub account to push malicious code to its backend, taking some users' names and emails; vaults weren't accessed (Zack Whittaker/TechCrunch)
